note: Sidecar, NOT yet merged into scripts/module-contracts.json. The build preflight (scripts/module-contract-preflight.mjs) asserts that every module declared required for a surface has a matching <script> tag in every owned-stamped shell for that surface. Merging this entry BEFORE the product wiring lands would therefore fail the build by design. Manager A must move the `module` object below into scripts/module-contracts.json in the SAME change that adds the script tags to the servable shells.

module.classRationale: Absence changes displayed OHLC values on every daily and weekly bar (wrong 24h window, wrong bar dates, missing Friday bar). Per §A4c this is a correctness-class dependency, not a performance one.

dependsOn.why: Sole source of instrument identity for the product path. chart.currentSymbol holds a display label (EURUSD_FULL_1MIN_1MIN, 20251028_194229_GBPUSD, EUR/USD, FILE_1234, null), and this registry already resolves those shapes for P&L. classFromRegistry gates on isRegistered() so an unrecognised label yields null rather than a guessed FX session.
dependsOn.absenceBehaviour: resolveIdentity returns {instrumentClass:null, cacheable:false, reason:'registry-unavailable'}; callers keep legacy epoch alignment, announce 'SessionCalendar.unresolved-instrument', and MUST NOT memoise the null. A transiently-absent registry must not become permanently absent.

registryGaps.note: Symbols the product can display that isRegistered() rejects, so the wired chart keeps epoch alignment for them. market-calculations.js is NOT in this packet's writable set; listed for whoever owns it.

misclassified.why: None is spot FX. DXY/USDX are index quotes; XTIUSD (WTI) and XNGUSD (natural gas) are energy contracts whose real session is CME 18:00 America/New_York, not 17:00. Wiring gives them the FX session. Recorded, not fixed — the registry is not writable here.

suffixStripping.mechanism: _resolveRegistryKey splits on / - _ . and whitespace and tries the longest segment. Separator-delimited suffixes therefore already resolve; bare alphanumeric suffixes do not, and '#' is not in the split set.
suffixStripping.belongsIn: the registry resolver (_resolveRegistryKey), NOT the session-class mapping
suffixStripping.rationale: EURUSDm and EURUSD are the same instrument for every consumer of the registry — pip size, P&L, margin, and session alike. Fixing it in classFromRegistry would give the session calendar a symbol vocabulary the P&L path does not share, which is how two normalisation rules drift apart. One resolver, one vocabulary.

indicatorSurface.why: The anchoring audit expects SessionCalendar to serve indicators, at which point the FVG's 18:00 ET and the Weekly Map's Monday-ET stop being private constants. bucketStart/openLocalTime accept an explicit `anchor` in place of an instrument class; namedAnchors() declares both, status 'declared'.
indicatorSurface.warning: fvg-18-et is 18:00 America/New_York and disagrees with the FX session open by exactly one hour. That disagreement is real and is NOT reconciled here.

sites.note: Third site, named by the anchoring audit and not by the original finding. Its tfToMs accepts d and w, so it floors daily and weekly to the UTC epoch too. SEPARATE ROW.

externalAuthority.rule: FX closes Friday 17:00 America/New_York, reopens Sunday 17:00 America/New_York, DST-aware via zoneinfo; docstring explicitly rejects the naive UTC weekday check.
externalAuthority.agreement: EXACT. Over 2013-2015 at minute resolution: 156 closes and 156 reopens, every close is a daily session open, every reopen is both a daily and a weekly session open, and every weekly open this module produces is a server reopen instant. Single local anchor Sunday 17:00 throughout. Zero disagreement.

killSwitch.name: __TALARIA_DISABLE_SESSION_CALENDAR_V1
killSwitch.offBehaviour: Every bucketStart call returns Math.floor(t / timeframeMs) * timeframeMs — byte-identical to pre-fix output for every timeframe.

labelConvention.barTimestamp: the session OPEN instant (FX: 17:00 America/New_York, DST-aware)
labelConvention.displayName: the session DATE, which is the open's local date plus labelOffsetDays
labelConvention.worked: A bucket opening Sunday 17:00 ET is NAMED MONDAY; a bucket opening Thursday 17:00 ET is NAMED FRIDAY.

instrumentIdentity.rejectedReason: Zero assignments in chart.js. A wiring reading these resolves an empty symbol, falls through to epoch alignment and changes nothing in the product while the oracle passes.
instrumentIdentity.confidenceGate: MarketCalculationEngine.isRegistered() — an explicit registry row. detectMarketType() alone is unusable here because it defaults to 'forex' for unrecognised labels, which would apply a 17:00 New York session to unidentified data.
instrumentIdentity.unresolvedBehaviour: Keep legacy epoch alignment for the affected timeframe AND announce 'SessionCalendar.unresolved-instrument'. Never guess.

notTouched: chart.js _resampleDataFull monthly branch (^(\d+)mo$) — already correct calendar months, byte-identity asserted by cell d

oracle.epsilon: 0 — exact equality. Fixture prices are dyadic rationals (1.25 + k/4096) and resampling performs only selection (first/last/max/min) plus integer volume sums, so no rounding can occur. Not a fitted tolerance.
